title: feat: install prints merge-on-green steps; PR text is checked
headline: Install prints every step only the owner can take to turn on merge on green, ready to paste and marked done or to do; the merge gate can arm again; and PR text, repo names and a command run from outside a project are held to the same checks as everywhere else.
alignment: v1.33.0 lands the owner's merge-on-green item and his rulings of 2026-11-15: every change only the user can make comes with exact steps, and the kit's own automation never lowers a standard it automates.

items.text: Install prints the merge-on-green steps ready to paste: the allow block, the grant with its git commands, the repo settings and the branch protection for both shells. Each is marked done, to do, or not checked with why.
items.before: A rule to read and lines to work out
items.after: Each step printed, ready to paste, marked done

items.text: PR text is checked where it is written: a PR needs a title and body file that pass the PR-body audit and name check. A typed body, stdin, gh api or another spelling is held; repo names are checked too. Descriptions are not.
items.after: Held unless it passes its audit

items.text: One title standard for commits, PRs and repo names: the plain result, as merged, with no internal tracking code. Shared tech names such as SHA256, UTF8 and S3 still pass.
A command that names a kit project from outside it runs that project's guards, in any spelling of its path or name, a wildcard, a brace list or $'' quoting included.
Status counts main as protected only with a required check that must be up to date, no force push and no delete, from branch protection or a ruleset; the protection template requires up to date.
items.after: Only what the merge gate needs

items.text: The merge gate can arm again: since 1.26.0 it read only the old hook shim and said no push hold on every project.
The PR-text audits run no program the repo's git config names and fetch nothing, since the guard runs them inside a hook.
The merge gate's PowerShell allow lines carry the full path with forward slashes, since the PowerShell tool never runs a $HOME path unasked.

The merge gate and status count up to date only from a source that also requires a check, read the rules 100 to a page, and name no repo when origin pushes somewhere else; check refuses a PR number with a leading zero, as disarm does.
Run install user and install project together: a project on 1.33.0 reads its PR checks from the user layer, and holds every PR until install user has run.

verification: Each code change has a test that fails on the code before it; the arm, template, PowerShell and status bugs were first reproduced live on a throwaway repo.
Recall on keys v11, five candidate runs on the final rule text scored blind with the baseline: candidate median 13, baseline (1.32.0) 13, control 0.

decisions.decision: The owner writes the allow lines and the grant
decisions.why: Each is the owner's own act: install prints them and marks each done when it finds it, and the repo settings are outward acts.

decisions.decision: PR text is held, not asked
decisions.why: A failing title or body goes out with neither a yes nor the bound: an ask would let a tap send text no audit passed.

decisions.decision: A named project fails toward checking
decisions.why: A reader of moves always misses a spelling, so any command that names a kit project runs its guards; a name in a command costs one more check, never a pass.

decisions.decision: Run install user and install project together
decisions.why: A project layer on 1.33.0 with a user layer on 1.32.0 holds every PR, because the audits it runs live in the user layer; the message says to run install user.

dimensions.name: Privacy
dimensions.result: Not touched: no personal data read or sent

dimensions.name: Code security
dimensions.result: Two highs (repo config programs in the audits, guards skipped from outside a project) and five mediums, all fixed

dimensions.name: Gaps, scaling, test value
dimensions.result: One high (an untested bound) and the test trims, the name allow-list and the layer note, all fixed

dimensions.name: Alignment
dimensions.result: YES; three highs on the printed steps from the owner's phone, all fixed

fixed: The audits ran programs the repo's git config names. Fixed in 508444d and cd0f9f5.
A command could work in a kit project from outside it with none of its guards. Fixed in 2ecbbde, 211b859 and eb1deaa.
The bounded-open test no longer tested the bound. Fixed in 4b0c3a1.
The printed steps missed the Free-plan limit, the track file content and the exact commands. Fixed in c12e39d.
accepted: A body file swapped between the guard check and gh reading it: CI and the merge gate re-read the body GitHub holds (the owner, 2026-11-15).
An admin can bypass the required check on main: by design for a solo owner (the owner, 2026-11-15).
A repo description and homepage are not audited, only its name (the owner, 2026-11-15).

tests.flips: declared tests on main and on this branch; the PR run gives the final count
